title: Implementation and module checks
goal: Connect command parsing to the model module and verify that an update reaches lookup and the report.

prerequisites.text: Use the previous lesson’s rules and recall the difference between a header and a translation unit.

terms.title: Module interface
terms.definition: The shared types and function declarations. Here they live in inventory.h.

terms.title: Translation unit
terms.definition: One preprocessed .c source file with the contents of its included headers.

sections.title: The parser recognizes a command and the model updates a record
paragraphs: A team lead asks to correct a zero in the stock list. Pass only the parsed ID and quantity into inventory_set. The function finds an existing record and writes the new value there. The main program owns command parsing.

Inventory is declared in inventory.h, which both main.c and inventory.c include. Pass both .c files to the compiler. The header supplies the types and declarations. The implementation in inventory.c is needed by the linker.

A model check creates an Inventory directly in memory and tests operations without any files. An integration check then runs text commands to confirm that the same invariant holds after reading records.tsv.

sections.title: Trace a command from stdin to the record
paragraphs: First look up the last item, which has zero stock. Then look up an unknown ID and update the actual record. Point to the step where main receives a success result from inventory_set.
inventory_find receives read-only access through a pointer to const Inventory. inventory_set receives a mutable Inventory because it updates the selected record.
steps: inventory_find returns a pointer to record 20. The interface prints 20 0.
For find 99 the model returns NULL. Processing still reaches the next command.
For set 20 7 the model returns 1 and the interface prints ok. The next lookup returns 20 7.

sections.title: A model check without file data
paragraphs: Build this main.c in place of the regular entry point, together with inventory.c. The after line shows that the first record stayed the same and the second was updated.

sections.title: Where to look for the cause
paragraphs: If the compiler sees the declarations and the linker points at inventory_find, inspect the source list. Add inventory.c and keep #include "inventory.h" in both units. A data error happens only after a successful build.

sections.title: Test your prediction with a new input
paragraphs: Check an update to the last element and look it up again. Separately check an unknown ID and compare every quantity before and after. The array state and the response text are different observations.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Compare the listed C17 rules with their use in this project.

selfcheck.prompt: Where is quantity changed for set 20 7?
feedback: The header declares types and functions.
The model finds the existing record and changes its quantity.

selfcheck.prompt: The stdin command set 20 7 printed missing. How can you check the model independently?
options: Rerun the same commands against a larger file.
Construct an Inventory containing record 20 in memory, call inventory_set and check for return 1 and quantity 7.
Replace missing with ok to check the remaining commands.
feedback: File loading, parsing and the model would still be tested together.
The direct call isolates the model. If it passes, inspect loading and parsing next.
Only the message changes. The model could still be wrong.

selfcheck.prompt: Why do the data for item 20 stay the same after set 99 6 and find 20? Give the response to each command.
selfcheck.feedback: Set looks for 99 only in the occupied part of the array. It changes nothing and prints missing. Find returns record 20 with its original quantity.

practice.title: Updating the last item on a shelf
practice.task: Implement inventory_set in inventory.c using the starter inventory for items 14 and 72. Update only existing IDs. Test the last record first and then a missing record. The build needs main.c and inventory.c.

steps.action: Read inventory.h, build and run the starter.
steps.why: The model already finds records and the temporary set always rejects the update.
steps.expected: set 72 8 produces missing where you expected ok.

steps.action: Return 1 only after updating the matching record.
steps.why: A success response should correspond to an actual update.
steps.expected: A subsequent find 72 yields 72 8 and an unknown ID still yields missing.

criteria: The first and last records remain searchable. Only the requested record changes after the update.
ok and missing separate success from absence. With report the artifact includes the updated quantity.
practice.hint: Compare your loop with inventory_find. Assign stock->records[i].quantity and return 1 after the assignment.

exercises.title: One more check
exercises.task: In a separate native folder, build a short main.c that constructs an Inventory in memory and calls inventory_set. Observe 1 for a present ID and 0 for an absent one. Compare both quantities as well.
criteria: Write your prediction before running. Compare stdout, stderr, status and files.

teaching.scene: Separate command parsing from inventory storage. Identify where the quantity changes and use a second lookup to prove that it changed.

predict.prompt: In the loaded example, item 20 has quantity 0. Predict the lines from find 20, find 99, set 20 7, and find 20 again. Which operations change the state?
predict.answer: The lines are 20 0, missing, ok, and 20 7. The first and last searches read the same item in different states. Only a successful set changes its quantity. No report file appears without report.

apply.prompt: In a fresh run of the same example, send set 10 0, find 10, and find 20. How will you tell that the update touched only one record?
apply.answer: The lines are ok, 10 0, and 20 0. Initially item 10 had 5 and item 20 already had 0. Track the IDs as well as quantities: matching quantities do not make two items one record.

practice.strategy: State what the function should return for a found or missing ID. Verify that the scan reaches the last item and that a missing ID changes nothing. Build main.c with inventory.c.
practice.diagnosis: If the first item updates but 72 still has quantity 0, inspect whether the scan returns after the first nonmatching item. If linking cannot find inventory_set, check the build inputs.

syntax.form: int inventory_set(Inventory *stock, int id, int quantity);
syntax.explanation: The header gives the caller argument and return types. The caller can print ok or missing from the return status. The actual field update belongs in inventory.c.
syntax.mistake: An ok line alone does not prove the value was stored. Follow it with a lookup or compare the report.
